topic: Semiparametric efficiency and cross-fitted one-step inference for the smooth quadratic conditional-optimal-transport lower bound on mean squared individual treatment effects in observational studies: extend Lin-Gao-Blanchet-Glynn (arXiv:2602.20681, Proposition 3.3 and Theorem 3.2) from randomized marginal-sample asymptotic normality to i.i.d. observational data under ignorability and overlap by deriving the observed-data canonical gradient, efficiency bound, propensity-corrected wavelet-Brenier one-step estimator, uniform studentized normality and Wald coverage, with Ji-Lei-Spector's 401(k) SIPP analysis as the applied consumer

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the observed-data canonical gradient and an efficient cross-fitted one-step estimator for the sharp smooth quadratic conditional-OT lower endpoint on mean squared individual treatment effects under ignorability and overlap.

source_refs.claim: Proves a quadratic-COT CLT for randomized marginal samples and explicitly leaves covariate-dependent propensity scores and observational ignorability as future work.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Gives an observational cross-fit AIPW construction for estimated OT dual functions, but not the canonical gradient or efficiency bound of the sharp smooth primal COT endpoint.
source_refs.author: Wenlong Ji, Lihua Lei, and Asher Spector

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the current inference statement with an explicit endpoint-value influence expansion and a one-step estimator
adding the endpoint LP derivative score to a sample LP value can double-count its first-order perturbations

open_problems.why_unsolved: Lin et al.'s first-order expansion uses independent randomized treatment-arm samples, whereas the observational law adds treatment-assignment, propensity, conditional-outcome, and covariate tangent directions. Ji-Lei-Spector supply inverse-propensity augmentation for fitted OT dual bounds, but weak-duality slack may remain and their theorem does not identify the efficient score for the sharp smooth primal endpoint. The prior CausalSmith attempt exposes a second concrete obstacle: naively adding an endpoint derivative score to a plug-in optimized value can count the same first-order perturbation twice. A solution must jointly differentiate the conditional Brenier value, project it onto the observed-data tangent space, and make the one-step correction cancel rather than repeat the plug-in derivative.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A pathwise-differentiability theorem giving the observed-data canonical gradient and efficiency bound, plus a cross-fitted one-step asymptotic-linear expansion with an explicit second-order remainder and consistent variance estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction supplies the exact partial-identification-to-COT-to-smooth-inference narrative and ends at the observational extension.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Individual treatment-effect moments are partially identified -> covariates sharpen their bounds through COT -> smooth quadratic COT admits randomized-sample inference -> observational efficiency requires a propensity-corrected canonical gradient and one-step estimator

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its cross-fit AIPW summand for fitted OT dual potentials and its product-rate remainder argument to the sharp smooth primal value.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest existing observational-data correction for a covariate-assisted causal OT bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Use smooth strongly convex Brenier-potential stability to linearize squared Wasserstein plug-in values and control their second-order remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Lin et al.'s conditional expansion builds on this smooth unconditional OT linearization.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine a Neyman-orthogonal score with cross-fitting and product-rate nuisance control to prove asymptotic linearity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the COT gradient is derived, its observational implementation is a multi-nuisance DML problem.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one prove a boundary-uniform von Mises remainder bound for an unregularized causal conditional-OT endpoint when its derivative is singular near a propensity-support boundary?

source_refs.excerpt: the boundary-scale plug-in remainder cannot be obtained from standard sqrt(n)-Donsker + Hadamard

open_problems.why_unsolved: The archived OT-boundary proposal found that the endpoint derivative scales like the inverse square root of distance to the propensity boundary. Standard Hadamard differentiability plus a global Donsker rate therefore does not force the second-order plug-in remainder to be negligible at the boundary scale; imposing the needed empirical-path rate directly merely assumes the desired conclusion. The same obstruction becomes relevant to observational quadratic COT if overlap is allowed to deteriorate rather than being bounded by a fixed constant.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A weighted OT-functional differentiability theorem with a primitive empirical-process norm and explicit uniform remainder rate, together with a regime statement separating root-n Gaussian inference from a boundary-local limit.

writing_exemplar.why: It is the archived proposal's direct OT-endpoint anchor and cleanly exposes the gap between an endpoint rate and limit/coverage theory.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal bounds are conditional-OT values -> propensity-support boundaries receive disproportionate weight -> ordinary functional delta methods lose uniform remainder control -> weighted OT differentiability must determine the valid inference regime

method_exemplars.technique: Regularize an OT endpoint to obtain differentiability and tractable limit theory, then quantify regularization bias.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the natural regularized benchmark against which an unregularized boundary-remainder theorem can be stated.

method_exemplars.technique: Localize estimation at a support boundary and derive the normalization and limit from tail regular variation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The causal OT remainder is dominated by a support-edge region, making frontier localization structurally analogous.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what smoothness, fixed-overlap, nuisance-rate, and variance conditions does the studentized observational quadratic-COT one-step statistic obey a uniform normal approximation and yield uniformly valid Wald coverage for the sharp lower endpoint?

source_refs.claim: Establishes a pointwise quadratic-COT CLT and suggests plug-in or bootstrap variance estimation, but not a uniform studentized theorem over observational laws.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Obtains uniform lower-confidence validity for randomized experiments, while its observational extension assumes estimated propensities bounded away from zero and one and can retain conservative dual slack.
source_refs.author: Wenlong Ji, Lihua Lei, and Asher Spector

open_problems.why_unsolved: Pointwise asymptotic linearity does not control coverage uniformly when smoothness radii, overlap, nuisance tuning, or the influence variance vary across data-generating laws. Ji-Lei-Spector's weak-duality construction can protect a possibly conservative confidence bound, whereas exact two-sided Wald inference for the sharp smooth endpoint requires uniform control of the primal stability remainder, every cross-fitting interaction remainder, the estimated Brenier-potential variance, and the lower tail of the studentizing denominator. Existing results do not assemble those controls for observational COT.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform studentized central limit theorem over an explicit observational smoothness-and-overlap class, with uniformly consistent standard errors and a Wald interval coverage theorem.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly frames the distinction among sharpness, nuisance robustness, conservative validity, and uniform coverage in the same COT partial-identification setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Covariates tighten partial-identification bounds -> flexible nuisance fitting threatens coverage -> weak duality restores robust but potentially conservative validity -> sharp observational COT requires uniform studentized Wald inference

method_exemplars.technique: Use uniform cross-fitted score expansions, moment envelopes, nuisance-rate sequences, and variance bounded away from zero.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the standard route from an orthogonal causal score to uniform Gaussian approximation with learned nuisances.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its uniform confidence-bound and observational AIPW arguments while replacing weak-duality slack with the smooth primal expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest COT paper combining uniform inference, cross-fitting, and observational propensity correction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use separately cross-fitted nuisance estimates to obtain fast doubly robust remainder rates for average conditional functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform Wald coverage hinges on making the multiple COT nuisance products uniformly negligible.

open_problems.open_problem: What inference procedure remains valid uniformly at and near the degeneracy frontier where treated and control conditional outcome laws coincide and the first-order efficiency bound for the quadratic COT endpoint vanishes?

source_refs.claim: Remark 3.2 states that asymptotic variance is positive iff the conditional laws differ on a positive-probability covariate set; at equality the estimator is faster than root n.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Shows that empirical Wasserstein functionals can have nonstandard directional limits and that the classical bootstrap can fail, motivating derivative-aware resampling.
source_refs.author: Max Sommerfeld and Axel Munk
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: Lin et al.'s Gaussian inference requires positive first-order variance, but the lower endpoint is zero when the two conditional laws coincide and its first derivative then vanishes. Along observational local alternatives approaching that equality set, inverse-propensity weighting, estimated conditional Brenier maps, and the changing order of the OT functional interact; neither root-n Wald inference nor an ordinary bootstrap is automatically valid. Existing Wasserstein degeneracy theory is largely unconditional or finite-support and does not incorporate ignorability, cross-fitted propensity correction, and conditional transport simultaneously.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A regime theorem giving the correct normalization and limit law at equality and under local alternatives, plus an adaptive confidence procedure valid in both the regular positive-variance regime and on the zero-variance frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Its positive-variance iff statement isolates the exact boundary at which its ordinary Gaussian inference ceases to apply.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Smooth quadratic COT has a first-order Gaussian law -> its variance measures separation of conditional potential-outcome laws -> equality makes the first-order law degenerate -> inference must adapt across the separation frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Apply a second-order delta method and a modified bootstrap when the first derivative vanishes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At coincident conditional laws the first-order derivative of squared COT vanishes, matching its first-order-degeneracy template.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive a transport functional's directional derivative and use resampling adapted to its nonstandard limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats Wasserstein inference at equality, though the desired result must add conditional transport and observational scores.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate and bootstrap the directional derivative rather than applying the ordinary bootstrap to the original functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An adaptive regular/degenerate COT procedure may require directional rather than ordinary differentiability near equality.

literature_map:
Lin-Gao-Blanchet-Glynn (2026, arXiv:2602.20681) establish smooth-density wavelet estimation, quadratic COT stability, and a pointwise CLT for randomized marginal samples.
Their conclusion explicitly names covariate-dependent propensity scores and observational ignorability as the next extension.
Their Remark 3.2 identifies a separate nonregular frontier: variance is positive iff conditional laws differ on a positive-probability set and vanishes at equality.
Ji-Lei-Spector (2024 revision, arXiv:2310.08115) develop model-agnostic OT-dual inference and an observational cross-fit AIPW correction.
Ji-Lei-Spector obtain robustness and uniform lower-confidence validity, but imperfect outcome models can leave conservative weak-duality slack rather than efficient inference for the sharp endpoint.
Their 401(k) SIPP application uses cross-fitted elastic-net propensities and AIPW dual bounds, connecting the observational theory directly to the requested empirical consumer.
Lin-Gao-Blanchet-Glynn (2025, arXiv:2506.00257) show direct COT plug-in inconsistency under weak topology and restore consistency using adapted-Wasserstein continuity, but do not supply observational efficiency theory.
Manole-Balakrishnan-Niles-Weed-Wasserman (arXiv:2107.12364) provide smooth Brenier stability and centered CLTs for squared Wasserstein plug-in estimators.
Niles-Weed-Berthet (arXiv:1902.01778) give minimax smooth-density estimation rates in Wasserstein loss and show the importance of densities bounded away from zero.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, DOI 10.1111/ectj.12097) provide the orthogonal-score and cross-fitting template for observational causal inference with ML nuisances.
Newey-Robins (2018, arXiv:1801.09138) sharpen cross-fit doubly robust remainder rates for average conditional functionals.
Sommerfeld-Munk (2018, JRSSB), Fang-Santos (2019, ReStud), and Chen-Fang (arXiv:1901.04861) supply nonregular and first-order-degenerate bootstrap machinery.
Crump-Hotz-Imbens-Mitnik (2009, Biometrika) and Hong-Leung-Li (2020, Econometrics Journal) show why overlap constants must enter observational variance and uniformity statements.
The live gap is the intersection: no located paper combines sharp smooth quadratic COT, the observed-data canonical gradient, efficient cross-fitted propensity correction, uniform studentization, and adaptive handling of the zero-variance frontier.
